baseline_summary: Baseline = classic DWA derived for the diff-drive AMR: state (x,y,theta,v,omega); Vs=[-0.5,2.0] m/s x [-1.5,1.5] rad/s; dynamic window Vd = v_a +/- a_v*dt_c, omega_a +/- alpha_w*dt_c with dt_c=0.05 s (a_v=1.0 m/s^2, alpha_w=2.0 rad/s^2 from config/robot_params.yaml) giving +/-0.05 m/s and +/-0.10 rad/s; admissibility replaced by collision-free rollout over T_sim = clip(v/a_v+0.5, 1.5, 3.0) s (braking distance v^2/2a = 2 m at 2 m/s). Sampling 11 x 31 = 341 + brake + spin candidates; exact arc integration with dt_s=0.1 s (<=30 poses); 3-stage costmap footprint check (centre cost >=253 -> collision; < circumscribed cost -> free; else FootprintCollisionChecker::footprintCostAtPose over the 0.60x0.40 m polygon, LETHAL=254). Cost J = w_h*heading + w_c*clearance + w_v*velocity + w_p*path + w_o*oscillation, each normalised to [0,1] (heading to a speed-dependent lookahead point; clearance from inflation cost inverted to distance; path = mean cross-track / 0.8 m band). Complexity O(M*N_t*P) ~ 4e5 cell reads worst case, ~2-3 ms per 20 Hz cycle on one core. Verified in the image: Nav2 1.1.20 nav2_core::Controller API (configure/setPlan/computeVelocityCommands/setSpeedLimit), only nav2_core::PlannerException exists in Humble, DWB critics and MPPI ObstaclesCritic/CostCritic are costmap-only (no obstacle velocity), teb_local_planner has no Humble binary (must be source-built), collision monitor stop/slowdown/approach semantics, BT replanning at 1 Hz, cmd_vel chain cmd_vel_nav -> velocity_smoother -> cmd_vel, Gazebo Sim 6.18 actors have no physics collisions (GT-based collision metric needed).

proposals.name: PVT-DWA (Probabilistic Velocity-obstacle & Time-to-collision DWA) — full plugin
proposals.idea: Three-stage nav2_core::Controller: (A) prune the sampled dynamic window with truncated VO (humans/forklifts) and ORCA half-planes (fleet AMRs, responsibility 1/2) using the exact chord velocity v*sinc(omega*tau/2) of each arc sample; (B) for every rollout pose, propagate each tracked obstacle with a CV model and covariance Sigma_j(t)=Sigma_pp + t^2 Sigma_vv + q t^3/3 I, and evaluate a closed-form collision-probability upper bound P_kj <= Phi((R_j - |mu|)/sigma_a), sigma_a = sqrt(a^T Sigma a), against a 2-circle robot cover; hard-reject samples with P >= delta_hard, and add a probabilistic TTC cost (first time P >= delta_ttc) plus joint-risk cost 1 - prod(1-P_kj); (C) standard normalised DWA costs plus a 0.8 m cross-track hard band (spec: <=1 m deviation), an always-present braking candidate, and weight scheduling for <=5 s return. Safety layering via setSpeedLimit (Warning zone), nav2_collision_monitor (0.3 m stop / 0.5 m slowdown / approach TTC) and an E-stop mux downstream; replanning via PlannerException after 5 invalid cycles plus the BT 1 Hz replanner.
proposals.closest_prior_work: Missura & Bennewitz ICRA 2019 (deterministic predictive DWA) + Zhu & Alonso-Mora RA-L 2019 (linearised Gaussian chance constraint); DRA-MPPI IROS 2025 (MC joint collision probability in MPPI); MD-DWA IEEE TWC 2026 (Mahalanobis-distance DWA for UAV); MCTS-VO 2025 (VO pruning); NH-ORCA DARS 2010.
proposals.expected_gain: Versus Nav2 DWB/MPPI (costmap-only, react to current occupancy): earlier and smaller avoidance manoeuvres against 1.0-1.5 m/s obstacles, expected to meet 0 collisions / <=1 m deviation / <=5 s return; versus deterministic predictive DWA: fewer near-misses when prediction uncertainty grows (sigma ~0.6 m at 2 s) without freezing, because margins scale with covariance instead of fixed inflation; deterministic runtime and per-term explainability for peer review.
proposals.risks: Depends on tracker publishing covariance and radius (amr_msgs/TrackedObstacle lacks them today); over-conservatism if q or delta are mis-tuned (freezing in S4 random-walk scenario); VO pruning may remove all samples (mitigated by fallback to full set); TEB comparison may fail if source build against Nav2 1.1.20 breaks; actor lack of physics in gz-sim 6 forces a ground-truth geometric collision metric.
proposals.realtime_budget: 343 samples x <=25 poses x 2 circles x <=10 tracks ~ 1.7e5 erfc evaluations (3-5 ms) + static footprint checks (1-2 ms) + VO (<0.1 ms) ~ 5-8 ms per 20 Hz cycle on one core (<=16% of the 50 ms budget); five robots ~ one core total.

proposals.name: Analytic probabilistic-TTC critic (Stage B alone)
proposals.idea: Standalone cost/validity term that can be added to the baseline DWA (or ported as a DWB TrajectoryCritic): time-parameterised Gaussian collision-probability upper bound along the rollout with CV covariance propagation and latency compensation, yielding TTC_delta and a joint-risk cost; no VO stage.
proposals.closest_prior_work: Missura & Bennewitz 2019 with Sigma=0 is the deterministic special case; Zhu & Alonso-Mora 2019 chance constraint; Safe Horizon MPC (de Groot 2023/IJRR 2025) for the joint-probability idea.
proposals.expected_gain: Most of the collision-avoidance gain of PVT-DWA at ~3-5 ms extra per cycle; serves as ablation A1 and as a drop-in for the team's baseline DWA if Stage A proves unnecessary.
proposals.risks: Half-plane bound saturates at 0.5 when the mean is inside the collision disc (handled by the hard check); independence assumption in the joint-risk product over-estimates risk for slowly varying errors.
proposals.realtime_budget: ~3-5 ms per cycle (1.7e5 normal-CDF evaluations); scales linearly with number of tracks, capped at the 10 nearest.

proposals.name: Chord-velocity VO/ORCA pruning of the dynamic window (Stage A alone)
proposals.idea: Map each (v, omega) sample's arc to the holonomic velocity of its chord over horizon tau (direction theta + omega*tau/2, magnitude v*sinc(omega*tau/2)), test membership in truncated VO cones (humans/forklifts, radius inflated by kappa*sigma) or ORCA half-planes (fleet AMRs), and skip rollouts for members; fall back to the full set if everything is pruned.
proposals.closest_prior_work: Fiorini & Shiller 1998 VO; van den Berg 2011 ORCA; NH-ORCA (Alonso-Mora 2010) effective-centre mapping; MCTS-VO (Bonanni 2025) showing VO pruning speeds search.
proposals.expected_gain: Satisfies the spec's 'VO or ORCA reactive avoidance' requirement explicitly, removes 20-60% of rollouts in crowded scenes (compute headroom), and provides a geometric explanation for reviewers; not expected to improve safety on its own beyond Stage B.
proposals.risks: Over-conservative in dense scenes (Park et al. ICRA 2026) — hence pre-filter only; chord mapping is exact only at the horizon endpoint.
proposals.realtime_budget: 343 x 10 quadratic root evaluations, <0.1 ms per cycle.

evaluation_plan: Metrics mapped to the spec: collisions (30 runs, 0) measured geometrically from ground-truth poses (robot footprint polygon vs actor circle / forklift-AMR box, 10 Hz, because gz-sim 6 actors have no physics contacts); path deviation (<=1 m) as max cross-track error vs the global path during avoidance; return time (<=5 s) from t_clear (all TTC_delta = inf) to 1 s sustained cross-track < 0.10 m; CTE 5 cm straight / 10 cm curved on obstacle-free segments; response time; compute time p50/p99 of computeVelocityCommands; jerk RMS and sign reversals. Log formats follow the spec's tables. Scenarios (6 x 5 seeds = 30 runs per algorithm): S1 perpendicular crossing person 1.0 m/s; S2 head-on forklift 1.5 m/s in 3 m aisle; S3 overtaking person 0.3 m/s; S4 two random-walk persons 0.5-1.2 m/s; S5 forklift on 4 m radius curve; S6 person crossing before a 0.6 m (robot width + 20 cm) narrow aisle. Baselines: Nav2 DWB, Nav2 MPPI, TEB source-built (ros2-master, include_dynamic_obstacles on/off if costmap_converter builds), and the team's static-only DWA. Ablations: no VO stage, deterministic TTC (Sigma=0, reproduces Missura 2019), no hard chance check, no deviation band. Success: PVT-DWA meets all three spec thresholds and shows significantly larger minimum distance than ablations (paired Wilcoxon per scenario, alpha 0.05); report mean +/- std, failure videos/logs. Tuning order documented: straight-line CTE (w_p, N_omega) -> curves (lookahead, w_h) -> S1 (delta_hard, w_t) -> S4 (q person) -> S6 (inflation, margin) -> 5-robot CPU <= 80%.
implementation_plan: Language C++17 in src/amr_navigation (ament_cmake, currently Python-only skeleton). Pure library amr_dwa_core (ROS-independent, gtest-covered): dynamic_window.hpp, rollout.hpp (exact arc integration, adaptive T_sim), footprint_checker.hpp (3-stage check on Costmap2D*), obstacle_model.hpp (CV prediction, covariance propagation, 2-circle cover, class table), velocity_obstacle.hpp (chord velocity, truncated VO, ORCA half-plane), collision_prob.hpp (Phi upper bound, TTC_delta, joint risk), critics.hpp (normalised heading/clearance/velocity/path/oscillation). Plugin library pvt_dwa_controller implementing nav2_core::Controller (verified Humble 1.1.20 signature), exported via pluginlib (plugins/pvt_dwa_plugin.xml, PLUGINLIB_EXPORT_CLASS(amr_navigation::PvtDwaController, nav2_core::Controller)); configured as controller_server FollowPath plugin at controller_frequency 20 Hz. Interfaces: subscribe /<ns>/tracked_obstacles (amr_msgs/TrackedObstacleArray, map frame, transformed to the local costmap frame via tf2) and fleet robot states; publish debug dwb_msgs/Trajectory2D + MarkerArray + a status topic (avoidance_active, TTC_min, n_valid); consume speed_limit via setSpeedLimit; throw nav2_core::PlannerException after 5 consecutive invalid cycles (only exception type in Humble). Local costmap 12x12 m @0.05 m, obstacle_layer observation_keep_time 0.0, inflation 0.8 m / scale 3.0, rectangular footprint. cmd_vel chain: cmd_vel_nav -> velocity_smoother (same accel/jerk limits from robot_params.yaml) -> nav2_collision_monitor (stop 0.3 m polygon, slowdown 0.5 m x0.3, approach time_before_collision 1.5 s; must be added to launch since Humble bringup does not include it) -> estop mux -> /cmd_vel. Message change: add position_covariance[4], velocity_covariance[4], radius, class_name to amr_msgs/TrackedObstacle (fallback defaults sigma_p 0.1 m, sigma_v 0.3 m/s with a one-time warning). All weights/delta/q/r_j in config/pvt_dwa_params.yaml (no rebuild). Unit tests (>=70% coverage): dynamic window bounds and brake candidate; rollout vs analytic arc endpoint (1e-9); footprint 3-stage on synthetic costmaps; VO known-geometry TTC and chord sinc limit, ORCA symmetry; collision probability vs 1e5-sample Monte Carlo (upper bound holds, gap < 0.03) and TTC_delta monotonicity in Sigma; critic normalisation; timing test p99 < 15 ms for 343x25x10; pytest for evaluation metrics. Compute budget 5-8 ms per cycle on one core. Schedule: W1 core+tests, W2 plugin+static comparison vs DWB, W3 tracks + Stage B/A, W4 safety chain + scenario scripts, W5 TEB build + 30-run evaluation + tuning, W6 ablations + report + peer-review documentation.
open_questions: TEB on Humble: teb_local_planner has no Humble binary (verified on index.ros.org and in the image); can the ros2-master branch plus costmap_converter be source-built against Nav2 1.1.20 in a separate Dockerfile stage, and if not, is MPPI acceptable as the optimisation-based baseline with a documented gap against the spec's TEB requirement?

Perception interface: will amr_msgs/TrackedObstacle gain position/velocity covariance, radius and class_name fields (or a parallel vision_msgs/Detection3D publication)? Without them PVT-DWA falls back to class defaults and the covariance-aware benefit cannot be evaluated honestly.

Dynamic-obstacle physics in Gazebo Sim 6.18: actors have no collision bodies (gz-sim issue #1364 open), so collision must be judged from ground-truth poses; should human obstacles instead be physical capsule models with a velocity plugin so contact sensors and LiDAR behave consistently?
Angular acceleration limit alpha_w = 2.0 rad/s^2 comes from config/robot_params.yaml, not the spec; it must match the URDF/DiffDrive plugin limits and the velocity_smoother configuration.

Fleet coordination: the ORCA responsibility-1/2 assumption requires all AMRs to run the same plugin; how does it interact with the fleet manager's intersection priority and deadlock resolution (option: raise responsibility to 1.0 for lower-priority robots)?

Where do the safety-zone manager (Warning zone -> speed_limit 50%) and E-stop mux live (which package/agent owns them), and is the collision monitor's 'approach' action allowed to slow the robot below the DWA's chosen speed without confusing the progress checker?

Missura & Bennewitz 2019 abstract was obtained through a search index rather than the PDF body; a team member should read the PDF to confirm the exact form of their dynamic collision model before the peer-review write-up.
